messages:
harper (product): Quick follow-up thread from today's all-hands pricing segment. Keeping it tight  post one-line Qs or clarifications and we'll reply.
jules (support): Do we proactively prevent long-running jobs from draining trial credits, or just notify? Customer support needs to advise.
sam (finance): We notify at 50/80/95% by default and can optionally block new jobs when trial hits 0. Blocking is configurable per-account.
noah (eng): Technical: for streaming calls we try to let the current chunk finish. If credits hit zero mid-stream we return a terminal message with a small footer explaining the reason and a 402 code on the final frame.
lin (ops): Ops note: there is an org setting `auto_block_on_zero` (false by default). Sales can request it be enabled for POCs or enterprise trials.
jules (support): What's the difference between "block" and "safety-hold"? Customers get confused.
lin (ops): Block is an automated enforcement that denies new requests. Safety-hold is an ops-triggered state (usually manual) for suspected abuse or anomalous traffic; it requires ops to review and lift.
harper (product): For SDKs: which headers should clients rely on to implement graceful shutdown and UI warnings?
noah (eng): Use `X-Credit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`, and `X-Model-Served`. On 429 include `Retry-After`. We added `X-Estimate-Cost` for previewing per-request cost in cents.
sam (finance): Pricing note: if we fallback to a smaller model mid-request due to capacity, billing reflects the model that generated the tokens. We include a per-request breakdown in the usage export.
jules (support): Refund question: if a customer accidentally runs a stress test and burns $2k in trial credits, is that usually credited back?
sam (finance): Typically yes for first-time genuine mistakes under a reasonable threshold. We prefer issuing credits on the next invoice; refunds to card are reserved for special cases.
harper (product): Another quick one: can project-level budgets be set so a runaway project doesn't use org credits?
lin (ops): Yes. Project budgets are supported and default to inherited org pool. Admins can enable `project_isolation: true` to silo credits per project. Migration tool exists for large orgs.
ops-bot: notice: "Quota policy updated for org __example__: on_zero=block"
jules (support): Last: any planned UI changes to make prepaid vs promo credits more visible? Customers complain the console is confusing.
harper (product): Yes, product is working on a clearer wallet UI with separate lines for promo, prepaid, trial, and SLO credits and a toggle to prefer prepaid for bursts. ETA next sprint for a beta.
sam (finance): For enterprise: we can negotiate rollover or custom grace windows in contracts. Default public behavior stays simple: month-bound trials/credits do not roll over.
harper (product): Ok thanks all. If you need a formal RFC or follow-up doc, react with :eyes: and I'll create one.
